newsitem.title: GERMANY: German blue-chip DAX index ends floor trade higher.
newsitem.headline: German blue-chip DAX index ends floor trade higher.

text.p: Germany's 30-share DAX index advanced strongly over bourse trade on Tuesday, heartened by an upbeat close on Wall Street overnight and the stable dollar against the mark to end at higher levels.

At the end of bourse trade the DAX index of 30 German blue-chips stood at 4,363.09 points, up 29.96 points, while the September DAX future contract was also in positive territory, up 62.5 points at 4,392/5 points.
"Volumes are very thin today, and I reckon we will probably see fairly strong resistance at around 4,400 points," a Frankfurt trader said.
"The way things have gone on the DAX recently, everything is possible on the upside," the dealer said.
The German share market saw its lowest volumes since mid-June on Monday, and the dealer said there was no reason to expect a major pick-up in volumes on Tuesday.
"Buying interest is very selective this morning," the trader said.
Among the shares favoured during electronic trade was the retailer Karstadt AG, which was among the top gainers in bourse and ended up 13.50 marks at 711.50 marks.
The Schickedanz retail group said that it planned to buy stakes in Karstadt held by Deutsche Bank AG and Commerzbank AG, but said its aim was not to take over the firm.
The move was viewed positively by the markets.
Other shares in the news included Henkel KGaA which ended up four marks at 104.50 marks after it released interim results.
Henkel's pretax profit rose 10 percent to 438 million marks from 397 million in the first half of 1997, while group sales rose to 9.784 billion marks from 8.039 billion marks.

Otherwise the main drivers behind the DAX index were the banks. Bankgesellschaft Berlin ended up 3.15 marks at 51.90 marks, Deutsche Bank AG was up 2.30 marks at 119.70 marks and Dresdner Bank AG was up 2.20 marks at 83.70 marks.
